ts-discriminated-unions-exhaustiveness.promptSeed:
Define a generic discriminated union and exhaustive state formatter:

### `type AsyncState<T>`
- Discriminated by `status`:
  - `{ status: 'idle' }`
  - `{ status: 'loading' }`
  - `{ status: 'success'; data: T }`
  - `{ status: 'error'; error: Error }`

### `formatState<T>(state: AsyncState<T>): string`
- Uses a `switch` statement that returns:
  - `'Idle'` for `'idle'`
  - `'Loading...'` for `'loading'`
  - `'Loaded: ' + JSON.stringify(state.data)` for `'success'`
  - `'Failed: ' + state.error.message` for `'error'`
- In the `default` branch, assigns `state` to a variable of type `never` (`const _exhaustiveCheck: never = state; throw new Error(...)`), ensuring unhandled statuses fail compilation.

loading
success serialises its data
error shows the message
Compile time: unknown status is rejected
testCases.expected: TS2345 — Argument of type '{ status: "oops"; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'AsyncState<unknown>'

testCases.description: Compile time: forgetting a case
testCases.input: add { status: 'cancelled' } to AsyncState without a case
testCases.expected: TS2322 — Type '{ status: "cancelled" }' is not assignable to type 'never' (in the default branch)

ts-generic-api-client.promptSeed:
Implement a type-safe HTTP client wrapper and custom error class:

### `class ApiError extends Error`
- Has numeric property `status: number`.
- `constructor(status: number)` calls `super(\`Request failed with status \${status}\`)`, sets `this.name = 'ApiError'` and `this.status = status`.

### `apiGet<T>(url: string): Promise<T>`
- Fetches `url`.
- For non-2xx responses (`!res.ok`), throws an `ApiError(res.status)`.
- On success, returns the parsed JSON cast to `T` (`(await res.json()) as T`).
- Network failures propagate unchanged.

testCases.expected: { userId: 1, id: 1, title: 'delectus aut autem', completed: false }

testCases.description: Non-2xx rejects with an ApiError carrying the status

ts-generic-component-props.promptSeed:
Define a generic component prop interface and rendering function where TypeScript enforces type parity across items and value:

### `SelectProps<T>`
Interface with the following properties:
- `items: T[]` — array of options.

ts-mapped-modifiers-deep-readonly.promptSeed:
Define advanced TypeScript mapped types using modifier removal (`-readonly`, `-?`), key remapping (`as`), and a runtime helper:

### `DeepReadonly<T>`
- Recursively marks all properties of object or array `T` as `readonly` (preserving functions as-is).

### `Mutable<T>`
- Removes `readonly` from all direct properties of `T`: `{-readonly [P in keyof T]: T[P]}`.

### `Concrete<T>`
- Removes the optional modifier (`?`) from all direct properties of `T`: `{[P in keyof T]-?: T[P]}`.

### `Getters<T>`
- Remaps property keys using `as` to produce getter method signatures (e.g. `{ name: string }` becomes `{ getName: () => string }`).

### `makeGetters<T extends Record<string, any>>(obj: T): Getters<T>`
- Runtime function that returns an object where each key in `obj` has a corresponding `get<Prop>()` method returning its current value.

ts-assertion-functions.promptSeed:
Implement TypeScript type guards and assertion functions to contrast boolean predicates with control-flow narrowing assertion signatures:

### `isDefined<T>(val: T | null | undefined): val is T`
- Type predicate returning `true` if `val !== null && val !== undefined`; returns `false` for `null` or `undefined`.
- Allows `if (isDefined(x)) { ... }` branches to narrow `x` to `T`.

### `assertDefined<T>(val: T, message?: string): asserts val is NonNullable<T>`
- Assertion function that verifies `val` is neither `null` nor `undefined`.
- If `val === null || val === undefined`, throws a `TypeError` with `message` (or default `'Value is null or undefined'`).
- If valid, returns `void`. In TypeScript, this narrows `val` in the remaining control flow to `NonNullable<T>` without an `if` block.

### `assertCondition(condition: unknown, message?: string): asserts condition`
- General invariant assertion function.
- If `condition` is falsy (`!condition`), throws an `Error` with `message` (or default `'Assertion failed'`).
- In TypeScript, asserts truthiness of the condition expression for subsequent lines.

### `assertRecord(val: unknown, message?: string): asserts val is Record<string, unknown>`
- Verifies `val` is a non-null plain dictionary object and not an array.
- If `val === null || typeof val !== 'object' || Array.isArray(val)`, throws a `TypeError` with `message` (or default `'Value is not a record object'`).
- If valid, returns `void` and narrows `val` to `Record<string, unknown>`.

testCases.description: isDefined returns true for values and false for null/undefined
assertDefined passes valid values and throws TypeError on null/undefined
assertCondition throws on falsy values with custom message
assertRecord validates plain records and throws TypeError on arrays/primitives

ts-tuple-rest-parameters.promptSeed:
Implement variadic tuple types and positional rest parameter utilities to manipulate strongly typed parameter lists:

### `type Concat<A extends readonly any[], B extends readonly any[]>`
- Concatenates two tuple types `A` and `B` into a single combined tuple `[...A, ...B]`.

### `type Shift<T extends readonly any[]>`
- Extracts a tuple with the first element removed. If `T` has at least one element, returns `Rest` from `[any, ...infer Rest]`; if `T` is empty `[]`, returns `[]`.

### `tuple<T extends any[]>(...elements: [...T]): [...T]`
- Creates and returns a tuple with its exact literal/positional element types preserved, avoiding implicit array widening (e.g. `tuple(1, 'a', true)` produces `[number, string, boolean]`).

### `partialApply<Leading extends any[], Trailing extends any[], R>(fn: (...args: [...Leading, ...Trailing]) => R, ...head: Leading): (...tail: Trailing) => R`
- Accepts a function `fn` expecting positional arguments `[...Leading, ...Trailing]`.
- Binds the leading arguments `...head: Leading`.
- Returns a new function that takes strictly the remaining `...tail: Trailing` positional arguments and returns `R`.

### `callWithTuple<Args extends any[], R>(fn: (...args: Args) => R, args: [...Args]): R`
- Executes `fn` by spreading the tuple arguments `args` in position.

testCases.description: tuple constructs a typed tuple without widening to arbitrary array
partialApply binds leading arguments and returns function for remaining arguments
callWithTuple executes function by spreading tuple elements
testCases.input: callWithTuple((a: number, b: number, c: number) => a * b + c, [3, 4, 5])

testCases.description: Concat and Shift tuple type contracts compile and verify lengths
